messages.subject: summarise with and without na.rm
parts:
Can someone suggest a dplyr idiom that allows na.rm to apply differently to different columns?

> library(dplyr)
> irisx <- iris
> irisx[1,1] <- NA
> irism <- ( irisx
+          %>% group_by( Species )
+          %>% summarize( Sepal.Length=mean( Sepal.Length, na.rm=TRUE )
+                       , Sepal.Length2=mean( Sepal.Length )
+                       )
+          )
> str(irism)

messages.author: 59e7d8d24bd426b2
messages.subject: Re: summarise with and without na.rm
parts:
Hi, 

irisx %>% group_by( Species )%>% 
  summarize( Sepal.Length1=mean(Sepal.Length,na.rm=F )
  , Sepal.Length2=mean(Sepal.Length, na.rm=T )
  , Nobs =length(Sepal.Length1)
  )

I think the problem is that you assigned the same name (Sepal.Length) to the first mean - so the second was the mean off the first, and not of the raw data.

Alain
